attribution.note: Ed Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, endorsed.

semantics.note: The sentence's main point is normative (about coverage), but it states two checkable facts as premises: the $157B valuation and burning $5B+ a year. The proposition captures these. The environment and 'real meaning' parts are opinion and are rightly not graded.

contract.note: Reading 'burns $5B+ a year' as OpenAI's 2024 net loss is a fair, ordinary reading: in Nov 2024 the widely reported figure was a ~$5B loss for 2024. A strict cash-burn reading is possible, but it is not the plain one, and no full-year cash figure is available anyway.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own funding announcement (Oct 2024) gives a $157B post-money valuation. It is a company disclosure, but it is the primary record of the round's terms.
CNBC report, before the post, that OpenAI expected about a $5B loss in 2024. The contract accepts the company's projection.

June 2026 report, before the evaluation date: audited 2024 net loss attributable to OpenAI was $5.09B, verified by the FT. The documents came from the speaker, but the FT verified them, so this is not self-proof.

Secondary summary with several typos. It reports H1 2024 cash burn of ~$340M against a ~$3B H1 net loss. This matters only under a cash-burn reading. Its H1 net loss figure is consistent with a ~$5B annual loss.

reviews.rationale: Both factual premises hold on the contract's fair plain reading. The valuation was $157B post-money in Oct 2024 (e1). OpenAI's 2024 net loss was projected at ~$5B (e2) and later reported as $5.09B audited (e3). The low H1 cash burn (e4) does not apply under the plain reading. The opinion parts are not graded.
